title: 📘 UNIT 1: LANDFORMS OF AFRICA
notes:
Landform → a physical feature on the Earth's surface that forms the terrain of an area.

⛰️ Three major landforms → Mountains, Plateaus and Plains.

🏞️ Minor landforms → Hills, Gorges, Valleys and Basins.

🌋 Landforms result mainly from volcanic and tectonic processes and from internal and external processes.

⭐ Africa's major landform regions :-
1️⃣ African Alpine System
2️⃣ African Massif
3️⃣ East African Highlands and Rift System
4️⃣ Southern Africa Platform

🌍 Landforms influence landscapes, ecosystems, climate, human perception and human interaction with the environment.}

title: 🌋 1.1 OVERVIEW OF THE WORLD'S MAJOR LANDFORMS
notes:
Landforms are produced by both internal and external processes.

🔥 Internal processes → processes originating inside Earth.
Examples → tectonic plate movement and volcanic activity.

🌧️ External processes → processes acting on the Earth's surface.
Examples → erosion by water and wind.

⭐ Internal processes can push up mountains and hills, while external processes can create gullies, river valleys and gorges.

⏳ These processes generally take very long periods, sometimes millions of years.

📍 Example → the Abbay Gorge was cut deeply by long-term erosion and reaches about 1,000 m in depth in the area.

title: 🌍 1.1.1 CONTINENTS OF THE WORLD
notes:
Continents → the largest landmasses of the world.

🌎 Seven continents from largest to smallest :-
1️⃣ Asia
2️⃣ Africa
3️⃣ North America
4️⃣ South America
5️⃣ Antarctica
6️⃣ Europe
7️⃣ Oceania (Australia)

🌊 The landforms make up the continents, while the water forms the oceans. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

title: 🌊 1.1.2 OCEANS AND COASTAL LANDFORMS
notes:
Oceans → large areas of salt water between continents.

🌊 Five oceans :-
1️⃣ Arctic Ocean
2️⃣ Atlantic Ocean
3️⃣ Indian Ocean
4️⃣ Pacific Ocean
5️⃣ Southern Ocean

📊 Oceans cover about 71% of Earth's surface.

🌊 Pacific Ocean → largest and deepest ocean; covers about one-third of Earth's surface.

🏝️ Island → piece of land completely surrounded by water.

📌 Greenland → largest island in the world.

🌊 Peninsula → land surrounded by water on three sides and connected to the mainland on the fourth side.

🔗 Isthmus → narrow strip of land with water on both sides that connects two larger pieces of land.

📍 Example → Isthmus of Panama connects North America and South America.

title: ⛰️ 1.1.3 MOUNTAINS
notes:
Mountain → large elevated landform with steep sides and high peaks that stand out from surrounding land.

🔨 Formation → rock layers are pushed together by tectonic movement, forcing land upward.

🌋 Mountains can also form through volcanic activity when lava and other materials accumulate on the surface.

🌊 Valley → low area between mountains.

🏔️ Mount Everest → highest landform/peak described in the textbook; 8,849 m above sea level.

🏔️ Himalayas → mountain range extending through South and Southeast Asia.

🌏 Formation of Himalayas → collision of the Indian and Eurasian continental plates about 40–50 million years ago.

title: 🌾 1.1.4 PLAINS
notes:
Plain → large area of flat, low land with little or no hills and mountains; an area of low relief with a relatively flat surface.

⭐ Importance :-
🌾 Crop cultivation
🐄 Animal husbandry/ranching

📍 Example → Great Plains of the central United States. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

title: 🏞️ 1.1.5 PLATEAUS
notes:
Plateau → large area of raised land that is relatively flat on top.

🌋 Formation → may result from volcanic activity beneath Earth's surface.

🔥 When magma pressure is not strong enough to break through the crust, it may push the land upward and form a plateau.

📌 Plateaus may occur alone in otherwise flat areas or near other plateaus. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

title: 🌍 1.2 LOCATION AND RELATED FEATURES OF AFRICA
notes:
Africa → second-largest and second-most populous continent after Asia.

📐 Area → about 30.37 million km².

🌍 Africa covers about 6% of Earth's total surface area and about 20% of its land area.

👥 The textbook gives Africa's 2020 population as about 1.3 billion, approximately 16% of the world's population.

🧭 Boundaries :-
⬆️ North → Mediterranean Sea
↗️ Northeast → Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
➡️ East → Indian Ocean
⬅️ West → Atlantic Ocean

🌍 The Equator divides Africa into approximately two equal parts.

🌐 Africa has 54 recognized sovereign states.

title: 🌍 1.2.1 AFRICA AND THE EQUATOR
notes:
🌍 The Equator crosses Africa and divides the continent into northern and southern parts.

⭐ Because the Equator divides Africa almost equally lengthwise, some climatic and physical conditions in the north have similarities with those in the south.

📌 Examples given :-
🏜️ Sahara ↔ Kalahari
🌿 Maghreb ↔ Karoo
🌊 Mediterranean region ↔ Cape area

⭐ Africa's position across the Equator contributes to the continent's broad physical and climatic diversity.

title: 🌍 1.3 MAJOR LANDFORMS OF AFRICA
notes:
Africa has several recognizable major landforms that form distinct physiographic regions.

🌍 Four major landform regions :-

1️⃣ African Alpine System → Atlas Mountains

2️⃣ African Massif → Sahara, Sahel, Savanna and Tropical Rainforest

3️⃣ East African Highlands and Rift System → Rift Valley and African Great Lakes; Ethiopian and Eritrean Highlands

4️⃣ Southern Africa Platform → Mountains and Desert Systems of Southern Africa

⭐ Landforms affect climate, ecosystems and human-environment relationships.

title: 🏔️ 1.3.1 AFRICAN ALPINE SYSTEM — ATLAS MOUNTAINS
notes:
Atlas Mountains → major mountain system of North Africa.

📍 Extends from Morocco to Tunisia.

⛰️ Main chains include :-
• Anti-Atlas
• High Atlas
• Middle Atlas
• Rif Mountains
• Tell Atlas
• Sahara Atlas

📏 Extends for more than 2,000 km from the Moroccan port of Agadir toward Tunis in Tunisia.

🌊 The mountains form a high divide between the Mediterranean Sea in the north and the Sahara Desert in the south.

🌍 The Atlas Mountains form an important part of the Maghrib region, including Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

title: 🏜️ 1.3.2 AFRICAN MASSIF — THE SAHARA DESERT
notes:
Sahara Desert → largest hot desert in the world.

📐 Area → about 9,200,000 km².

📍 Extends across North Africa from the Atlantic coast in the west to the Red Sea in the east.

🧭 North → Mediterranean Sea and Atlas Mountains.
⬇️ South → extends toward the Sahel.

🌍 Covers all or large parts of ten countries :-
Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan and Tunisia.

🏜️ Important desert surfaces :-
🔴 Erg → large sand sea made mainly of sand dunes.
🪨 Reg → desert pavement consisting of pebbles/gravel over a broad flat surface.

⭐ The Sahara is one of the major physical regions of the African Massif.

title: 🌾 1.3.2.1 THE SAHEL
notes:
Sahel → vast semi-arid transitional region immediately south of the Sahara.

📍 It forms a transition between the Sahara Desert and the more humid areas farther south.

📏 Extends for about 5,000 km as a broad savanna belt along the southern edge of the Sahara.

🗣️ Sahel comes from the Arabic word 'sahil', meaning shore or edge.

⭐ It is an important transition zone between desert and savanna environments. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}

title: 🌿 1.3.2.2 THE SAVANNA
notes:
Savanna → tropical grassland region with grasses and scattered trees, associated with seasonal rainfall and a pronounced dry season.

🌿 Two important vegetation parts described :-
1️⃣ Savanna woodland
2️⃣ Thorn-tree tall-grass savanna

🌳 Savanna woodland → trees are widely spaced because dry-season soil moisture is insufficient for continuous tree cover.

🌾 Open spacing allows grasses to form a dense lower layer.

🌳 Trees may have flattened or umbrella-shaped crowns, thick bark and adaptations to dry conditions.

🔥 Fires commonly occur during the dry season, and many tree species are fire resistant.

🦁 The region provides important habitat for wildlife and supports many parks.

title: 🌴 1.3.2.3 TROPICAL RAINFOREST
notes:
Tropical rainforest → occurs mainly near the Equator, both north and south of it.

🌳 Equatorial rainforest → highly diverse forest with many plant and animal species.

🌿 Broadleaf evergreen trees dominate.

🌳 Forest structure → closely spaced trees form a thick continuous canopy about 25–35 m high; some trees reach about 40 m and have buttressed bases.

🌱 Characteristic vegetation → evergreen trees, epiphytes, herbaceous plants, vines/lianas and ferns.

🌧️ Rainfall → more than about 2,000–2,250 mm annually and generally distributed throughout the year.

🌡️ Temperature and humidity → high throughout the year.

🌱 Heavy rainfall causes strong chemical weathering and leaching, making tropical soils acidic and nutrient poor.

title: 🌋 1.3.3 EAST AFRICAN HIGHLANDS AND RIFT SYSTEM
notes:
The East African Highlands and Rift System contains two major physical regions :-

1️⃣ Rift Valley and African Great Lakes
2️⃣ Ethiopian and Eritrean Highlands

⭐ The region is characterized by major highlands, tectonic features, valleys, lakes and volcanic landforms.

title: 🌍 1.3.3.1 RIFT VALLEY AND AFRICAN GREAT LAKES
notes:
🌋 East African Rift Valley → formed mainly through normal faulting.

⬇️ Graben → elongated block of Earth's crust between two faults that has moved downward relative to the blocks on either side.

📍 Rift Valley System → begins near the Red Sea, crosses Ethiopia, reaches the Lake Victoria region, divides into eastern and western branches, and continues southward through Lake Malawi toward Mozambique.

📏 Total length → about 5,600 km.
📐 Average width → about 32–80 km.

🌊 Rift Valley lakes extend from Ethiopia southward toward Malawi and include the African Great Lakes.

💧 Many lakes are freshwater and rich in biodiversity, while some are alkaline or saline.

📌 Lake Victoria → Africa's largest lake; it is not located on the floor of the Rift Valley but occupies a depression between the eastern and western rifts.

title: 🏔️ 1.3.3.2 ETHIOPIAN AND ERITREAN HIGHLANDS
notes:
🏔️ Ethiopian Highlands → extensive highland region with a central complex of mountains and plateaus.

🌋 The Great Rift Valley divides the central highland complex and separates northwestern and southeastern highland areas.

⬇️ Lowlands occur around the edges of the higher elevations.

⭐ Terrain diversity produces regional variations in :-
🌦️ Climate
🌿 Natural vegetation
🌱 Soil composition
🏘️ Settlement patterns

🇪🇹🇪🇷 Northwestern Ethiopian Highlands extend into Eritrea and reach elevations above 2,000 m.

📍 The Northwestern Highlands rise along the western scarp of the Great Rift Valley and extend northward toward the Red Sea.

title: 🏜️ 1.3.4 SOUTHERN AFRICA PLATFORM
notes:
Southern Africa → region south of the Congo and Tanzania.

⭐ Landscape includes :-
⛰️ Escarpments
🏔️ Mountains
🌿 Grasslands
🏜️ Deserts

♑ Tropic of Capricorn crosses the middle of the region, indicating that parts of southern Africa extend outside the tropics.

🏔️ Most recognizable feature → Ukhahlamba (Drakensberg) Escarpment.
📏 Average altitude → almost 3,000 m above sea level.

title: 🏜️ 1.3.4.1 KALAHARI AND NAMIB DESERTS
notes:
🏜️ Kalahari Desert → lies mainly in Botswana.

🌾 Landscape → mixture of arid grassland and sand.

🦌 When rainfall is sufficient, grasslands provide grazing for wildlife.

🦁 Kalahari contains game reserves and national parks.

🏜️ Namib Desert → located along the west coast of Namibia.

🌊 The Namib is influenced by the cold Benguela ocean current along the coast.

⭐ The textbook associates the formation of the Namib partly with the nearby cold ocean current. :contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}

title: 🌾 1.3.4.2 HIGHVELD AND GREAT ESCARPMENT
notes:
🏞️ Highveld → portion of the South African inland plateau.

⬇️ It slopes gently downward.

🧭 Bounded by :-
⬇️ South → Great Karoo
⬅️ West → Kalahari Desert
⬆️ North → Bushveld

🌾 Importance → one of South Africa's major commercial farming areas.
🏙️ It also contains a major concentration of metropolitan centers, particularly the Gauteng conurbation.

⛰️ Great Escarpment → separates the Highveld from KwaZulu-Natal in the south.

🏔️ Ukhahlamba/Drakensberg → southeastern portion of the Great Escarpment and forms the boundary between KwaZulu-Natal and Lesotho.

title: 🌍 LANDFORMS AND THE ENVIRONMENT
notes:
Landforms are not only physical features; they influence the environment and ecosystems.

⭐ Important effects :-

📐 Elevation, slope steepness and aspect → influence ecological potential.

🌱 Landform regions → influence the distribution and movement of organisms, energy and materials.

🔥 Landforms → affect spatial patterns of disturbances such as fire and wind.

🛡️ Landforms can resist geomorphic change and help protect biological features and processes.

🌦️ Landforms also influence climate at different scales :-

🌍 Macroclimate → climate over large areas.

📍 Microclimate → climate over smaller areas.

⭐ Ecosystems develop within landform regions and interact with their physical environment.

title: 🧠 UNIT 1 KEY TERMS
notes:
🌍 Landform → physical feature forming the terrain of an area.

⛰️ Mountain → high elevated landform with steep sides and prominent peaks.

🏞️ Plateau → raised land with a relatively flat top.

🌾 Plain → broad, flat, low-lying land.

🏔️ Hill → elevated landform smaller/lower than a mountain.

🌊 Valley → low area between higher land.

🪨 Gorge → deep, narrow valley produced by erosion.

⬇️ Basin → relatively low area surrounded by higher land.

🏝️ Island → land completely surrounded by water.

🌊 Peninsula → land surrounded by water on three sides.

🔗 Isthmus → narrow land strip connecting two larger land areas.

🌋 Internal processes → processes originating inside Earth.

🌧️ External processes → surface processes such as erosion by water and wind.

⬇️ Graben → down-dropped block of crust between faults.

🏜️ Erg → sand sea/dune-covered desert surface.

🪨 Reg → desert pavement of pebbles/gravel.

🌍 Macroclimate → climate of a large area.

📍 Microclimate → climate of a small area.

title: ⭐ UNIT 1 QUICK REVISION
notes:
📌 Three major landforms of the world → Mountains, Plateaus and Plains.

📌 Major landforms are mainly associated with internal Earth processes, while external processes modify the surface and form features such as valleys and gorges.

📌 Seven continents → Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Oceania.

📌 Five oceans → Arctic, Atlantic, Indian, Pacific and Southern.

📌 Africa → second-largest and second-most populous continent after Asia.

📌 Africa is bounded by the Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Indian Ocean and Atlantic Ocean.

📌 The Equator divides Africa into approximately two equal parts.

📌 Four major African landform regions :-
🏔️ African Alpine System
🏜️ African Massif
🌋 East African Highlands and Rift System
⛰️ Southern Africa Platform

📌 African Alpine System → Atlas Mountains.

📌 African Massif → Sahara, Sahel, Savanna and Tropical Rainforest.

📌 East African Highlands and Rift System → Rift Valley/African Great Lakes and Ethiopian/Eritrean Highlands.

📌 Southern Africa Platform → mountains and desert systems of Southern Africa.

📌 Sahara → largest hot desert in the world.

📌 Sahel → semi-arid transition zone south of the Sahara.

📌 Rift Valley → formed through normal faulting and contains a major chain of lakes.

📌 Lake Victoria → largest lake in Africa and lies in a depression between the eastern and western rifts rather than on the Rift Valley floor.

📌 Ethiopian and Eritrean Highlands → high plateau and mountain region divided by the Great Rift Valley.

📌 Southern Africa → includes the Drakensberg Escarpment, Kalahari Desert, Namib Desert and Highveld.

⭐ Core idea → Africa's diverse landforms result from long-term geological processes and create distinct physiographic regions that influence climate, ecosystems, drainage, vegetation and human activities.
